title: Redefine illumination delta and density tokens for compact UI
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: introduce a small, composable token axis that reconciles compact density requirements with accessible contrast and physically plausible shadow layering. This ticket scopes a focused revision for the 'compact' surface family used in action bars, data cards, dense tables, and small charts. We will define: a) multi-step delta tokens for illumination/penumbra (micro-elevation), b) bidirectional spacing/radius deltas (for dense vs. roomy modes), and c) a reduced typographic delta set intended for compact list and table rows.

Motivation: current token set is optimized for medium density and becomes visually noisy or indistinct at compact sizes. Teams report inconsistent shadows and cramped radii across small components; migration ad-hoc tweaks increase dev friction. Defining a systematic, documented compact axis will reduce per-component overrides and improve cross-surface coherence while preserving a11y legibility at small sizes.

Scope: token definitions, design tokens JSON examples, migration mapping for buttons/tables/charts, Figma token library update, engineering codemods for CSS/JS token keys, and rollout documentation for consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Compact token palette (color neutrals, accent reductions) exported as design-tokens JSON and validated in Figma variables
Three-step micro-elevation tokens (compact-elevation-1..3) implemented and visualized across: action chips, dense table rows, and data cards
Radius delta token family (compact-radius-small/medium/large) with interpolation guidance for avatars/buttons/containers
Typography deltas for small UI (compact-type-100/200) with WCAG AA contrast guidance for common foreground/background combos
Migration mapping doc that maps existing tokens -> compact tokens and a codemod spec for ENG to implement
Regression checklist and visual QA pages for charts, buttons, tables with before/after states
Design sign-off from PM (Priya Rao) and Accessibility review completed and documented
tasks: Audit current token usage in components (collect catalog of overrides and per-component custom shadows)
Define compact color neutrals and accent tone reductions; generate contrast matrix for small text sizes
Author compact micro-elevation tokens with penumbra/ambient layering specs and sample CSS variables
Propose radius interpolation curves and publish examples for avatar/button/container proportions
Create Figma library file and replace tokens in sample pages (cards, dense tables, chart legends)
Write migration playbook and codemod spec; coordinate with ENG for rollout windows
Run visual diffs for 4 key pages and capture accessibility snapshots
design_artifacts: Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/compact-token-assets (includes PNG previews, token JSON export)
engineering_notes: Implementation should expose tokens as --rwd-compact-elevation-1..3, --rwd-compact-radius-sm/md/lg, and --rwd-compact-type-100/200; fallbacks must map to existing --rwd-elevation-* keys for older consumers
Codemod spec: map legacy shadow tokens (e.g., --rwd-shadow-small) -> compact equivalents and surface classes; draft PR skeleton: github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/4721
Performance: prefer CSS variables + GPU-friendly shadow layering; avoid heavy box-shadow stacks on table rows to limit paint cost when many rows render
Charts: ensure legend contrast updated for compact tokens; check canvas drawing code uses color-token lookup rather than hardcoded hex values
Backend schemas: token names must remain stable; if renaming unavoidable, add aliasing layer in token loader to avoid runtime breakages
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design preview in Figma and internal review (Mar 8–15)
Phase 1: Token JSON export and feature-flagged ENG integration in staging (Mar 22–Apr 2)
Phase 2: Run codemod across UI monorepo with safe-rename commit and shadow toggle (Apr 5–9)
Phase 3: Internal beta with selected product pages + visual QA (Apr 10–17)
